title: How does a thread wait for another to end?
question: A thread joins another: it sleeps until the other exits. How does the kernel tell it (with no thread library in between)?
text: Call 1, [mem = mmap2(NULL, 65536, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0)](1): [do_mmap](1:do_mmap) Memory for the new thread's stack.

Call 2, [thread = clone(CLONE_VM | CLONE_FS | CLONE_FILES | CLONE_SIGHAND | CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_SYSVSEM | CLONE_CHILD_SETTID | CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID, mem + 65536, NULL, mem, 0)](2): [copy_process](2:copy_process) A new thread, told to write its tid at mem (CLONE_CHILD_SETTID), and to clear it and wake it when it exits (CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID).
Call 3, [futex_time64(mem, FUTEX_WAIT, thread, NULL)](3): [futex_do_wait](3:futex_do_wait) Join: wait while mem holds the thread's tid. The call blocks.
Call 4, [thread: exit(0)](4): [do_exit](4:do_exit) The thread exits. [futex_wake](4:futex_wake) Its memory's last use (mm_release): it clears mem and wakes a waiter on it: the join returns 0.

steps.name: thread
args: CLONE_VM | CLONE_FS | CLONE_FILES | CLONE_SIGHAND | CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_SYSVSEM | CLONE_CHILD_SETTID | CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID
